transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is my eating habits lately. 

After my late shifts, I’ll stop for takeout on the way back. I usually end up eating two burgers, fries, a shake... and then I'll still go home and clean out the leftovers in the garage fridge like it’s a second supper. It's just a lot of food, and I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
When you're eating all that food, does it feel like you can't control what you're doing or stop yourself from eating more than you intended?

Yeah, that's pretty much exactly it. It's like... once I start, it feels like a switch is flipped. I'll actually be sitting there telling myself, "Roy, just shut the bag and go inside," but my hands just keep reaching for more. I just can't seem to stop myself once I get going.
Does this eating behavior bother you or cause problems in your life, like feeling ashamed, guilty, or affecting your work or relationships?

Yeah, it definitely bothers me. Afterward, I just feel ashamed, really. And kind of disgusted with myself. I've always thought of myself as a pretty disciplined and dependable guy, you know? But doing this... it makes me feel like I'm sneaking around in my own house. It just feels like I'm really letting myself down.
After these episodes of eating a lot, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or doing a lot of exercise?

No, I don't do anything like that. I don't make myself throw up or take pills or anything. And after a long shift at the plant, I'm usually too tired to even think about exercising. I mostly just go to bed feeling uncomfortably full and pretty bad about myself.
Do you usually find yourself eating this way when you're feeling stressed, sad, or upset about something?

I'm not really sure if it's tied to a specific mood. I mean, work can be stressful, but I don't know that I only do this when I'm upset. It just seems to happen, mostly when I'm alone and the house is quiet. I haven't really noticed a pattern with how I'm feeling right beforehand.
How often would you say these episodes of eating a lot and feeling out of control happen—like, do they happen several times a week, once a week, or less often?

Well, for the past few months, it's been happening pretty regularly. I'd say there's usually at least one night a week where I end up doing this. And honestly, it's often more like two or three times a week, especially after a late shift or a rough day on the line.
When you have these episodes where you feel out of control with eating, do they happen all in one short period of time, like within a couple of hours?

Yeah, it all happens pretty fast. Definitely within a couple of hours. Like, I'll get off a late shift and stop for takeout on the way home, and I'll end up eating two burgers, fries, and a shake. But then I'll still go home and head straight to the extra fridge in the garage and just clean out whatever leftovers are in there. It's... it's almost like I'm having a whole second supper right after the first one, all in that same short window of time before I go to bed.
Do these eating episodes make it hard for you to function normally, like affecting your mood, your work, or how you interact with others?

Well, I'm still getting to work fine, and I keep up with church and all that. It hasn't stopped me from doing what I need to do. But... I guess I've been a lot more withdrawn at home lately. It just takes up a lot of energy, you know? Trying to cover up where I stopped on the way home, or trying to come up with excuses for why I'm not hungry for a regular dinner. So I just kind of keep to myself more to avoid the questions.
Do these eating episodes make you feel depressed or anxious, or do they seem to make any existing feelings like that worse?

Well, I don't know if I'd call it depressed, exactly, but... afterward, I definitely feel ashamed. And, honestly, just kind of disgusted with myself. 

I mean, I've always thought of myself as a pretty disciplined and dependable guy. I go to work, I do what I'm supposed to do. So doing this... feeling like I have to sneak around with food... it just makes me feel like I'm really letting myself down.
Do these eating episodes cause you significant distress, or affect your ability to function in any important area of your life, like your relationships, work, or social activities?

Well, kind of like I mentioned a little bit ago, work is fine. I haven't missed a shift, and I still keep up with church every week. It hasn't messed up those parts of my life. 

But... yeah, it definitely affects things at home. I've just been a lot more withdrawn from my family lately. It takes so much energy trying to cover my tracks, you know? Hiding where I stopped to eat, or making up reasons why I don't want a regular dinner with them. It's just easier to keep to myself so I don't get asked any questions.

Do these late-night eating episodes happen even when you aren’t feeling stressed, upset, or after not eating during the day, or do they seem to be linked to skipping meals or not eating enough earlier in the day?

Well, I don't really know if they're linked to anything specific like that. I mean, I eat normally during the day—I take my lunch to work, eat when everyone else does. And I wouldn't say I'm feeling particularly stressed or upset when it happens. It just... happens, I guess. I haven't really noticed a pattern with skipping meals or anything like that.
Do you often eat much more rapidly than normal, and keep eating until you feel uncomfortably full, even if you weren't really hungry to begin with?

Yeah, I do. When I'm out in my truck or out in the workshop, I eat so fast... half the time I barely even taste the food. It's really just like I'm trying to get it all down before somebody catches me.
Do you find yourself eating large amounts of food even when you’re not really hungry?

Yeah, I think I kind of just mentioned that, but... yeah. I'm not really hungry when I do it. Like I said, I eat my regular meals during the day, so my stomach isn't empty or anything when I go out to the truck. It's really not about being hungry at all.
Do you ever restrict your eating during the day or follow any strict diets before these episodes happen?

No, not at all. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I just eat my regular meals. I'm not on any kind of strict diet or... or trying to hold back on food during the day. I just eat a normal breakfast and have my regular lunch at work.
